quotes.text: Editing a draft is not the same as constructing the model of the problem in your head. Review optimizes for polish. Authorship optimizes for understanding.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints what teams lose when humans shift from authors to reviewers of AI drafts.

quotes.text: AI doesn't have to be right to become authoritative. It just has to be readable. Fluency is interpreted as competence.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Compact explanation of authority bias in AI-mediated work.

quotes.text: So here's the line you want to remember. Copilot can accelerate knowledge work. It cannot replace epistemic responsibility.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis on human accountability.

quotes.text: So the first principle is simple. Viva Insights is not a productivity scoreboard. It's a drift detector.

quotes.text: The irreplaceable human isn't the person who can write. It's the person who can be held accountable for a claim.

takeaways: Copilot is not a feature toggle but a participant that frames decisions, so judgment, context and accountability become more valuable, not less.
AI drafts, recaps and summaries raise output while eroding shared understanding unless teams protect epistemic agency and treat recaps as input, not truth.
Intentional friction — human-written problem statements, two alternatives, decision logs and visible AI contribution — keeps decisions owned and humans irreplaceable.
hook: Copilot makes your teams faster, but are they still making good decisions? This episode is for leaders rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot who want productivity gains without losing judgment, debate and ownership. You get a three-layer collaboration model and practical norms that keep humans accountable when AI is always in the room.
